name: Sumerian city-states
origin: Urbanisation of southern Mesopotamia into independent cities such as Uruk, Ur and Lagash
ending: Conquered by Sargon of Akkad
summary: Independent city-states, each centred on a temple and ruled by a priest-king or governor. They shared a culture and gods and fought over canals and borders.

name: Pharaonic Egypt
origin: Predynastic Egypt
ending: Conquest by the Roman Empire after the death of Cleopatra VII
summary: The king was a living god and head of the state religion. Priesthood, bureaucracy and ritual worked as one machine for roughly three thousand years.

name: Akkadian Empire
origin: Sargon of Akkad unites the Sumerian city-states
ending: Collapse under invasion and internal weakness; the causes are still debated
summary: Often called the first empire: one ruler over many cities, with Akkadian as a language of administration.

name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
origin: Kings begin campaigns that win back lost provinces
ending: Fall of Nineveh to Babylonians and Medes
summary: A standing army, mass deportation of conquered peoples and a net of provincial governors ran the largest empire of its day.

name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
origin: Cyrus the Great overthrows the Median king
ending: Conquered by Alexander the Great
summary: Provinces under governors (satraps), linked by a royal road, a standard tribute and a general respect for local law and gods.

name: Sparta
origin: Constitution traditionally credited to Lycurgus
ending: Forced into the Achaean League, which abolished its traditional institutions
summary: Two kings, a council of elders and five elected ephors governed a warrior citizen class that lived off the labour of enslaved helots.

name: Carthage
origin: A Phoenician colony grows into a trading power run by its leading families
ending: Destroyed by Rome in the Third Punic War
summary: Two annually elected suffetes, a senate of leading families and a citizen assembly governed a trading empire. Start date marks the rise of that system, not the city’s founding.

name: Roman Kingdom
origin: Traditional founding of Rome by Romulus
ending: Expulsion of the last king, Tarquin the Proud (traditional account)
summary: Seven legendary kings. The sources are much later and partly myth, so the dates are conventional.

name: Ancient Athenian Democracy
origin: Reforms of Cleisthenes
ending: Conquest by Macedon and a change of constitution
summary: Adult male citizens voted directly in the assembly and filled many offices by lot. Women, enslaved people and foreigners were excluded.

name: Roman Republic
origin: Overthrow of the monarchy
ending: Transition to the Roman Empire
summary: Annual magistrates (consuls), a senate of ex-magistrates and popular assemblies. It conquered the Mediterranean, then tore itself apart in civil wars.

name: Maurya Empire
origin: Chandragupta Maurya overthrows the Nanda dynasty
ending: The last emperor is assassinated by his general
summary: A centralised empire with a large bureaucracy and spy network. Ashoka later set out edicts on stone across the realm.

name: Hellenistic kingdoms
region: Eastern Mediterranean and the Near East
origin: Alexander’s generals divide his empire
ending: Absorbed by Rome; Ptolemaic Egypt was the last to fall
summary: Successor dynasties (Ptolemies, Seleucids, Antigonids) ruled older populations through Greek-speaking elites.

name: Imperial China
origin: Qin unifies the Warring States
ending: Abdication of the last Qing emperor after the 1911 revolution
summary: Dynasties rose and fell but the idea held: one emperor ruling by the Mandate of Heaven, served by a bureaucracy.

name: Roman Empire
origin: Octavian becomes Augustus
ending: Deposition of the last western emperor; the eastern half continued
summary: Rule by an emperor backed by the army, provinces run by appointed governors, and citizenship that spread outward over time.

name: Sasanian Empire
origin: Ardashir I overthrows the Parthians
ending: Conquered by the Rashidun Caliphate
summary: A Zoroastrian-backed monarchy with powerful nobles and clergy that rivalled Rome and Byzantium.

name: Byzantine Empire
origin: Permanent division of the Roman Empire
ending: Ottoman capture of Constantinople
summary: The Roman state continued in the East with Greek as its language, an autocratic emperor and an Orthodox church bound to the court.

name: Caliphate (Rashidun to Abbasid)
region: Middle East, North Africa and Iberia
origin: Death of Muhammad; Abu Bakr becomes the first caliph
ending: Mongol sack of Baghdad ends the Abbasid caliphate there
summary: Rule by the Prophet’s successor, joining religious and political authority. In practice power drifted to regional dynasties long before the end.

name: Papal States
origin: The Frankish king Pepin grants lands to the pope
ending: Annexed by Italy during unification
summary: The pope ruled as a worldly sovereign over a band of central Italy.

name: Feudalism
origin: Medieval Europe
ending: Centralization of power and development of nation-states
summary: Land held in exchange for service. Lords owed their lord loyalty and soldiers; peasants owed their lord labour.

name: Icelandic Commonwealth
origin: Founding of the Althing
ending: Chieftains swear allegiance to the Norwegian king
summary: No king and no executive: chieftains (goðar) and a yearly assembly that made and interpreted law.

name: Holy Roman Empire
origin: Otto I is crowned emperor in Rome
ending: Dissolved by Francis II after Napoleon’s victories
summary: An elected emperor over hundreds of semi-independent states, cities and bishoprics: close to a federation in everything but name.

name: Republic of Venice
origin: Election of the first doge (traditional date)
ending: Surrender to Napoleon
summary: A doge elected for life by a hereditary noble class whose Great Council held office for a thousand years.

name: Mongol Empire
origin: Temüjin is proclaimed Genghis Khan
ending: Split into khanates; the Yuan dynasty fell in 1368
summary: Among the largest land empires in history, tied together by a khan, a code of law and a relay-post system until it divided into four khanates. End date is the fall of the last, the Yuan.

name: Old Swiss Confederacy
origin: Three forest cantons swear a charter of mutual defence (traditional date)
ending: French invasion and the Helvetic Republic
summary: A growing league of self-governing cantons and allied towns with no single ruler.

name: Ottoman Empire
region: Anatolia, the Balkans and the Middle East
origin: Osman I founds a principality in Anatolia
ending: The sultanate is abolished; the republic follows in 1923
summary: A dynastic sultanate that governed religious communities through the millet system and a salaried military-administrative elite.

name: Aztec Triple Alliance
origin: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan ally against Azcapotzalco
ending: Spanish conquest and the fall of Tenochtitlan
summary: A tribute empire: conquered cities kept their own rulers and paid goods and labour to the allied capitals.

name: Inca Empire
origin: Pachacuti begins the expansion from Cusco
ending: Spanish conquest
summary: A labour tax (mit’a) and a road network held a state together that kept records on knotted cords (khipu) rather than in a conventional script.

name: Haudenosaunee Confederacy
origin: Five nations join under the Great Law of Peace; scholars date this anywhere from the 12th to the 15th century
ending: Still in existence
summary: Clan mothers nominate chiefs, and a Grand Council decides by consensus among the nations.

name: Absolute monarchy (Europe)
origin: Consolidating monarchies claim power from God, answerable to no parliament
ending: Rise of constitutional monarchies and republics; the Russian tsar falls in 1917
summary: The ruler claimed to hold power from God and to answer to no assembly. Louis XIV of France is the classic case.

name: Mughal Empire
origin: Babur defeats the Delhi Sultan at Panipat
ending: The last emperor is deposed by the British after the 1857 rebellion
summary: A Persianate court ruled most of South Asia through mansabdars, ranked officials paid from land revenue.

name: British Empire
origin: England claims Newfoundland
ending: Handover of Hong Kong to China
summary: A maritime empire of colonies, protectorates and dominions governed from London. Both ends are conventional markers.

name: Dutch Republic
origin: Act of Abjuration declares independence from Spain
ending: French revolutionary armies and the Batavian Republic
summary: A federation of seven provinces governed by merchant regents. The stadtholder was a hereditary military leader, not a king.

name: Ganden Phodrang (Tibet)
origin: The fifth Dalai Lama takes power with Mongol backing
ending: Flight of the 14th Dalai Lama after the 1959 uprising
summary: The Dalai Lama headed both monastery and state, served by lay and monk officials.

name: Tokugawa Shogunate
origin: Tokugawa Ieyasu is named shogun
ending: Meiji Restoration
summary: A hereditary military ruler governed Japan while lords (daimyo) ran some 250 domains under close supervision.

name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
origin: Union of Lublin
ending: Third partition among Russia, Prussia and Austria
summary: Nobles elected the king and could block laws in the Sejm: a noble “democracy” that left out most people.

name: Constitutional monarchy
origin: England’s Bill of Rights limits the Crown
ending: Still in existence
summary: A monarch whose powers are limited by a constitution or parliament. Present-day examples include the UK, Japan and Sweden.

name: United States (federal republic)
origin: The Constitution takes effect and Washington is inaugurated
ending: Still in existence
summary: A written constitution divides power between a federal government and the states, and among three branches.

name: First French Republic
origin: The monarchy is abolished
ending: Napoleon is proclaimed emperor
summary: Born in revolution. It was ruled by a Convention, then a five-man Directory and finally a Consulate.

name: Kingdom of Hawaiʻi
origin: Kamehameha I unites the islands
ending: Overthrow of Queen Liliʻuokalani by a foreign-backed committee
summary: A monarchy that adopted a written constitution in 1840.

name: First French Empire
origin: Napoleon crowns himself emperor
ending: Defeat at Waterloo
summary: A military-bureaucratic empire with centrally appointed prefects, a single legal code and satellite kingdoms across Europe.

name: Zulu Kingdom
origin: Shaka becomes chief of the Zulu
ending: Annexed by the British to Natal
summary: A centralised military monarchy built on age-regiments.

name: Imperial Japan
origin: Meiji Restoration
ending: Defeat in World War II and adoption of a new constitution
summary: An emperor on the throne, a modernising state and, from the 1930s, military dominance of government.

name: Confederate States of America
origin: Secession from the United States
ending: Defeat in the American Civil War
summary: A presidential confederation of eleven states whose constitution explicitly protected slavery.

name: Soviet Communism
origin: Russian Revolution
ending: Collapse of the Soviet Union
summary: One-party rule by the Communist Party over a state-owned economy.

name: Weimar Republic
origin: German Revolution and the Weimar constitution
ending: Hitler is appointed chancellor and democracy is dismantled
summary: A parliamentary democracy with a directly elected president, undermined by economic crisis and political violence.

name: Fascist Italy
origin: March on Rome
ending: Mussolini is deposed; a German-occupied puppet state followed until 1945
summary: A one-party state under Benito Mussolini, who took the title Duce.

name: Nazi Germany
origin: Rise of the Nazi Party
ending: Defeat in World War II
summary: A totalitarian one-party dictatorship under Adolf Hitler that carried out the Holocaust.

name: Francoist Spain
origin: Nationalist victory in the Spanish Civil War
ending: Franco dies and Spain moves to democracy
summary: A military-led dictatorship under Francisco Franco with a single legal party.

name: Apartheid South Africa
origin: The National Party wins the whites-only election
ending: First multiracial elections
summary: A white-minority government that legally separated people by race.

name: North Korea
origin: Division of Korea after World War II
ending: Still in existence
summary: A one-party state ruled by the Kim family since its founding.

name: People’s Republic of China
origin: Communist victory in the civil war
ending: Still in existence
summary: A one-party state led by the Communist Party of China.

name: Cuba
origin: The revolution overthrows Batista
ending: Still in existence
summary: A one-party socialist state in which the Communist Party is the only legal party.

name: Saudi Arabia
origin: Ibn Saud proclaims the Kingdom
ending: Still in existence
summary: A monarchy with no elected national legislature. Its Basic Law names the Quran and Sunnah as the constitution.

name: Islamic Republic of Iran
origin: The revolution overthrows the Shah
ending: Still in existence
summary: An elected president and parliament sit under a Supreme Leader who is a senior cleric.

name: Universal-suffrage democracy
origin: New Zealand gives women the vote, the first self-governing country to do so
ending: Still in existence
summary: Every adult citizen votes. Many countries now hold elections, though how free and fair they are varies widely.

name: European Union
origin: The Maastricht Treaty takes effect
ending: Still in existence
summary: Member states pool part of their sovereignty in shared institutions: a Commission, a Parliament and a Council.
